svg.text: TEACHER ANCHOR: CCSS.5.NF.A.1 • TEKS 111.7.b.3.H • UNSPSC 60101700 • TITLE I / IV GRANT ELIGIBLE • MODEL: SC6
LESSON GUIDE: COMMON DENOMINATOR ADDITION & EQUIVALENCE
Grades 3–8 Fractions & Proportional Reasoning • Hands-On Classroom & Home STEM Studio Series

g.text: STEP 1: SEAT 1/1 WHOLE IN REFERENCE WELL

text.tspan: Place the 84.00 mm Whole [1/1] block in the left reference slot.
This physical block establishes the 100% benchmark height.
Place one [1/3] block (28.00 mm) in the right comparison well.
Stack one [1/4] block (21.00 mm) directly on top of the [1/3].
Notice: neither thirds nor fourths alone measure this sum!
3. TEST COMMON TWELFTHS: Stack 7 twelfths: 7 × 7.00 mm = exactly 49.00 mm! Flush summit!
Calculator Verification: Press Fraction Display Icon ([FDISP] & [g][SIMP]) and run 1 [ENTER] 3 [÷] 1 [ENTER] 4 [÷] [+] [FDISP] → 7/12.

g.text: CORE PRINCIPLE: COMMON DENOMINATORS ARE COMMON SIZES

text.tspan: You cannot directly add thirds and fourths because their blocks are different physical heights!
Converting to twelfths (4/12 + 3/12 = 7/12) literally swaps disparate pieces for identical
7.00 mm unit blocks so their heights can be counted directly!

g.text: ★ NOW YOU TRY! (STUDENT PRACTICE CHALLENGE): ADD: 1/2 + 1/3

text.tspan: Seat [1/2] (42mm) and [1/3] (28mm) together. Test sixths: how many [1/6] blocks reach the exact 70.0mm summit? (Scan QR for 3D animated solution!)

g.text: → Build with your blocks, then scan the QR code to watch the animated 3D solution on your screen!
